name: Drostanolone

card.summary: Masteron: a DHT-derived injectable once used against breast cancer and now used by bodybuilders for a dry, hard look, with no appearance trials.
card.note: Historic breast-cancer drug; forum users raise hair-loss concerns, and its effects on appearance have not been studied.

quick.overview:
Drostanolone, widely known as Masteron, is an injectable anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone. Medically it was tested in the 1960s to 1980s as hormone therapy for advanced breast cancer. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as an add-on for a lean, dry, hard look and as a way to limit estrogen-related effects.

The only human trials found are in breast cancer. No published study has measured its effect on physique, face or skin in healthy users, so the claims on forums rest on user reports.
quick.mechanism: It is a 2-alpha-methyl derivative of DHT, so it activates the androgen receptor and is not converted to estrogen by aromatase. The propionate ester is the usual injectable form.[1][2]
quick.risks: Breast-cancer trials judged side effects generally not serious in that setting.[3] Forum users warn about hair loss in those predisposed, since DHT-derived compounds are not blocked by finasteride or dutasteride in their account, and about skin and cardiovascular effects of stacks.[4][5] It is detected in anti-doping controls and prohibited in sport.[6]

lead: Drostanolone, also called dromostanolone and best known by the brand name Masteron, is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone (DHT) with a methyl group added at the 2-alpha position. It is usually encountered as drostanolone propionate, an injectable ester [1][20][21].

In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing circles the appeal is appearance: users describe it as giving a harder, drier, more defined look when body fat is already low, and as a compound that adds muscle conditioning without being converted to estrogen, which proponents link with less water retention and with a sharper, more masculine look [5][11][20]. It is typically discussed as an add-on to testosterone or other compounds rather than a stand-alone product [4][11].

Medically, drostanolone propionate was used from the early 1960s to treat advanced breast cancer in women, under names such as Drolban and Masteril, and was studied in randomized trials from 1968 onward against oophorectomy, nandrolone, testolactone, ethinyl estradiol and tamoxifen [3][7][8][9][10][20][21]. It is no longer marketed for medical use [21].

No published study has tested drostanolone for cosmetic outcomes in healthy people. The human evidence consists of breast-cancer trials and anti-doping research, while community claims about physique, skin, hair and estrogen control come from user reports [3][6][10].

angle.text: Bodybuilders and some looksmaxxing forum users add it to a physique-focused regimen during a lean phase in the hope of a dry, hard, vascular look and a more masculine appearance. These effects are reported by users; no trial has measured them [5][11][20].

infobox: 1959; propionate introduced for medical use in 1961 [20][21]
US Schedule III; prohibited in sport; not currently marketed [20][21][2]

paras: Drostanolone propionate (Masteril) was tested in breast cancer in a trial from 1968 to 1972 against oophorectomy in premenopausal patients, nandrolone phenylpropionate in perimenopausal patients and ethinyl estradiol in postmenopausal patients; response rates were 44 percent versus 22 percent in the premenopausal group, 34.5 percent versus 39 percent in the perimenopausal group and 38.5 percent versus 57 percent in the postmenopausal group, and the authors described side effects as generally not serious [3].

Other randomized studies compared drostanolone with nandrolone, testolactone and testosterone decanoate, finding similar response rates, with added cyclophosphamide raising response rates in combination arms [7][8][9]. A 1982 French trial in 98 postmenopausal women found that hormonal therapy with tamoxifen plus drostanolone produced the best immediate objective responses and the fewest adverse effects compared with CMF chemotherapy or the combination [10]. Use declined as tamoxifen and later aromatase inhibitors became standard, according to Grokipedia, which also reports that the US approval was terminated in 1994 (a date the page itself gives inconsistently) [2].

In bodybuilding, drostanolone is associated with cutting phases, where users aim to preserve muscle and show conditioning as body fat falls; Wikipedia describes non-medical use for physique and performance enhancement, and Grokipedia says users favor it for muscle hardness and vascularity [20][2]. Users on a looksmax.org thread said it can look very good when lean [5].

Some forum users see it as relevant to facial masculinisation, arguing that DHT-type androgens support a more angular, masculine look [11]. Others ask whether it can be run alongside heavy skincare and retinoid routines to protect skin, and replies in that thread were mixed [4]. A fourth thread compared it with oxandrolone [13]. None of these claims has been tested in a trial.

Like other anabolic-androgenic steroids, drostanolone is an agonist of the androgen receptor. It is not a substrate for 5-alpha-reductase and a poor substrate for 3-alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, which Wikipedia says gives it a high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio (reported in rodents as roughly 1:3 to 1:4) [20]. The androgen receptor binds testosterone or DHT and regulates gene expression; in hair follicles DHT is the main androgen acting [23].

Because it is a DHT derivative it cannot be aromatized into estrogenic metabolites [20]. Grokipedia describes anti-estrogenic effects used historically in breast cancer; its actual effect on estrogen levels in users has not been shown in published trials [2]. It is not 17-alpha-alkylated, so it is not known to cause the liver toxicity linked with oral steroids, although Wikipedia notes that high doses or prolonged use could still harm the liver [20].

The propionate ester has near-zero oral bioavailability and is given by intramuscular injection; it acts as a prodrug and, per Wikipedia, has an elimination half-life of about 2 days [21]. Grokipedia gives 2 to 3 days and says metabolites leave mainly in urine as sulfate and glucuronide conjugates [2].

Drostanolone is 2-alpha-methyl-5-alpha-dihydrotestosterone (formula C20H32O2) [20]. Two crystal polymorphs of the propionate ester have been characterised by X-ray diffraction [1]. A methylated derivative, methyldrostanolone, has been identified in commercial products [15].

Drostanolone and its propionate were first described in 1959, in the same paper as oxymetholone and methasterone, and the propionate entered medical use in 1961, first in the United States and shortly afterward in Europe [20][21]. Grokipedia attributes development to researchers at Syntex [2]. Brand names over time included Drolban, Masteril, Masteron, Masterid, Permastril and others [21].

Clinical research in breast cancer ran through the 1960s to early 1980s [3][7][8][9][10]. After the drug left the medical market it continued to circulate through non-medical channels; Grokipedia says legitimate production had largely stopped by the late 1980s [2]. Surveys of competing bodybuilders in Flanders from 1988 to 1993 found 38 to 58 percent of controlled athletes positive for doping agents in some federations [19].

Clinical studies are limited to randomized breast-cancer trials from 1968 to 1982 comparing drostanolone propionate with oophorectomy, nandrolone, ethinyl estradiol, testololactone and testosterone decanoate, or combining it with tamoxifen or cyclophosphamide [3][7][8][9][10]. One 91-patient controlled trial compared testololactone, drostanolone and nandrolone in advanced breast cancer, recording remissions at 4 and 16 weeks [8]. A randomized comparison with testosterone decanoate and testololactone reported similar rates of objective response among the single hormone therapies [7]. No human study has examined drostanolone for appearance.

In breast cancer, randomized trials from the 1970s reported objective response rates of roughly a quarter to a half of patients depending on the comparison and whether chemotherapy was added, with no clear difference among the androgens compared [3][7][8]. No randomized trial has evaluated drostanolone for muscle, leanness, skin or facial appearance.

The breast-cancer trials reported that side effects were generally not serious and rarely contraindicated use in that setting [3]. Wikipedia lists virilization in women, acne, hair loss or accelerated male-pattern baldness, unfavorable cholesterol changes, possible liver damage and mood changes such as aggression and irritability [20]. Anabolic steroids as a class suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, which can cause testicular atrophy, reduced sperm production and hypogonadism, raise blood pressure and LDL cholesterol while lowering HDL, and can accelerate pattern baldness in predisposed men [22].

Forum users cite hair loss in genetically predisposed people, and one stated that finasteride and dutasteride do not counteract DHT-derived compounds [5]. Another user reported only bloating and mood changes on a testosterone-based regimen without an aromatase inhibitor [11]. One forum user said it is known to be harsh on lipids, and another said strong androgens and DHT derivatives are associated with a "flatness" feeling [24][28]. In a T Nation thread about female use, a poster wrote that drostanolone induced low rates of virilization relative to testosterone propionate; the class as a whole carries virilization risk for women [25][20].

A study of hamsters found that animals self-administered drostanolone, along with nandrolone, oxymetholone and stanozolol, into the brain ventricles, work used to study the reinforcing properties of anabolic steroids [14]. Compounds sold as drostanolone on the gray market have been analysed for adulteration by NMR [18].

Drostanolone is one of the most frequently detected anabolic androgenic steroids in doping control analysis [6]. Urinary metabolites have been characterised for detection, including long-term metabolites [6][16][17][15], and Grokipedia lists WADA prohibition under S1 anabolic agents and several suspension cases in sport [2]. Forum members discussing natural bodybuilding contests list drostanolone among compounds banned by such federations [27].

In the United States drostanolone, like other anabolic steroids, is a Schedule III controlled substance; Grokipedia ties this to the Anabolic Steroids Control Act of 1990, lists it as Class C in the UK, and Wikipedia lists Schedule IV in Canada [20][2]. It is prohibited in sport [2][6].

On looksmaxxing forums, drostanolone appears in the stacks of young and adult posters and in debates over whether DHT-derived androgens help or harm facial appearance and hair [4][5]. Some members say they favor it over aromatase inhibitors for managing estrogen-related effects; others on the same thread recommend other compounds or say an aromatase inhibitor is rarely needed [11]. Members of the TRT-focused T Nation forum say some clinics add DHT-derived steroids such as drostanolone to testosterone regimens [26].

timeline.event: Drostanolone and its propionate first described [20][21].
Drostanolone propionate introduced for medical use in the United States [21].
A South African trial of drostanolone propionate (Masteril) in breast cancer begins, running to 1972 [3].
Randomized comparisons with testosterone decanoate and testololactone in disseminated breast cancer are published [7].
Drostanolone propionate is compared with nandrolone decanoate in breast carcinoma [9].
A French randomized trial tests tamoxifen plus drostanolone against chemotherapy [10].
Doping-control sampling of Flemish bodybuilders begins, running to 1993 [19].
US Anabolic Steroids Control Act, which Grokipedia links to its Schedule III status [2].
New urinary metabolites identified for doping control [6].
Crystal polymorphs of drostanolone propionate characterised [1].

lore.intro: Drostanolone is discussed on looksmax.org and T Nation as a hardening, drying compound, as an estrogen-control add-on, and with recurring concern about hair loss and cholesterol [4][5][11][24].

claims.claim: Masteron gives a dry, hard, lean look.
claims.believers: Users say it makes a lean physique look sharper, one writing that you will look good if lean [5].
claims.experts: Published human trials are in breast cancer; no study has examined body composition or appearance with the drug [3][10].

claims.claim: Masteron can replace an aromatase inhibitor for controlling estrogen.
claims.believers: A user says forum members promote it for estrogen control and describes taking it in place of an aromatase inhibitor [11].
claims.experts: It does not aromatize itself, and Grokipedia says its effect on systemic estrogen is not clearly established; no trial has tested it for this purpose [20][2].

claims.claim: It may cause hair loss that finasteride cannot block.
claims.believers: One forum user warned that DHT-derived steroids can damage follicles depending on genetics and that finasteride and dutasteride do not work for them [5].
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists accelerated male-pattern baldness as a side effect, and DHT is the main androgen acting in hair follicles; no published study examines drostanolone and hair specifically [20][23].

claims.believers: A user says DHT has benefited him in masculinizing his face and that he has had no hair loss [11].
claims.experts: No published study has examined facial structure or skin in drostanolone users; anabolic steroids as a class are linked with acne, oily skin and pattern baldness in predisposed men [22].

claims.claim: Skincare and collagen products can offset the skin effects of a large steroid stack.
claims.believers: A young poster asked whether a collagen-preserving skincare stack would make a stack including Masteron worthwhile; others disagreed and recommended surgery instead [4].
claims.experts: No published research tests this combination.

claims.claim: It is gentler on women because it virilizes less than testosterone.
claims.believers: A T Nation poster wrote that drostanolone induced low virilization rates relative to testosterone propionate [25].
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists virilization in women among the drug's side effects [20].

claims.claim: It is hard on cholesterol and the heart.
claims.believers: T Nation posters describe lipid effects of drostanolone as dose-dependent and harsh [24].
claims.experts: Anabolic steroids as a class raise LDL, lower HDL and have been linked with hypertension and cardiac changes [22][20].
